title.en: The game that challenges the tiger

text.en: Hekko is a team game from Nagaland. Its name means challenging the tiger, and it comes from a folk story in which humans challenged the tiger Aakho. In this chapter you will read how Hekko is played, learn words that sound alike but are spelt differently, animal sounds, the past tense with -ed and irregular verbs, and identify traditional games from their descriptions.

In the Mokokchung district of Nagaland, people play a game called Hekko, a well-known sport today. Hek means to challenge and ko means tiger, so Hekko means challenging the tiger. A folk story tells of Aami, the man, and Aakho, the tiger. Long ago humans and animals lived together. They disagreed about who was superior, and Aakho declared that tigers had the first right on everything. The humans challenged Aakho, and that challenge became the game of Hekko.
Hekko is played between two teams, Aami and Aakho, with eleven players in each team. A toss decides which team will be Aami and which will be Aakho. A circle is drawn. The Aami team makes a human chain inside the circle, while the Aakho team stays outside. Two Aakho players enter and try to push the Aami players out of the circle. A pushed-out Aami player is out and cannot come back. The Aami team tries to catch the Aakho players by surrounding them. A caught Aakho player is held until he says Joko, which means surrender, and then another Aakho player enters. Each time a team gets an opponent out it earns points.
The game ends when all Aakho players are caught, or all Aami players are pushed out, or the time runs out. The team with the most points wins. The fastest Aami player gets the title Khozuba and the strongest Aakho player gets the title Khotiba. The game helps the village find its strongest people and teaches teamwork, strength and quick thinking.
Declared means said clearly and firmly. Superiority means being better or stronger than others. A disagreement is when people do not agree. To surrender means to give up. The word decide goes with the word decision.
Some words sound the same but have different spellings and meanings. There shows a place and their shows ownership. There is a park there. They finished their work. Two is the number 2 and too means also or very. Two friends joined. I was too tired. Threw is the past of throw, and through means from one side to the other. He threw the ball. I see clouds through the window. Caught is the past of catch and a cot is a small bed. Right is the opposite of left, and write means to put words on paper.
To tell about something that happened in the past we change the verb. Many verbs add -ed: visit becomes visited, jump becomes jumped, watch becomes watched. Some verbs change completely and are called irregular verbs: come becomes came, drink becomes drank, drive becomes drove, see becomes saw. Animal sounds: a tiger roars, a horse neighs, an elephant trumpets, a dove coos, a goat bleats and a monkey whoops.
In Lagori, seven stones are stacked, a team knocks them down with a ball and then tries to rebuild the stack while the other team tries to hit them. In Kabaddi, a raider crosses to the other side chanting kabaddi without taking a breath and tries to tag players and return. In Gilli-danda, a short stick is hit into the air with a long stick and then struck again, and the distance it travels is measured. Games with a small glass ball flicked at other glass balls are the game of marbles. Traditional games build strength, balance and teamwork, and skipping builds strong bones.
You can invent a new game: give it a name, say when it is played, how many players it needs, what equipment, and write simple rules. A good game has clear rules, is fair, and is safe for everyone.

problem.en: Choose the correct word: The bowler ___ the ball towards the batsman. (threw or through)

text.en: We need the past of throw.

why.en: Past action needs the past form.

text.en: Threw is the past of throw.

why.en: Through means from one side to the other.

text.en: So: The bowler threw the ball.

why.en: Check the meaning, not only the sound.

problem.en: Write the past of drive and jump.

text.en: Jump is a regular verb.
Jump becomes jumped.
Drive is irregular.

prompt.en: Explain what Hekko means, how it is played and who wins.

requiredIdeas.en: Hek means challenge and ko means tiger
Aami makes a human chain in a circle, Aakho tries to push them out
The team with the most points wins

points.en: Hekko is a team game from Nagaland that means challenging the tiger.
Aami stay in the circle and Aakho try to push them out.
Their and there, two and too, right and write sound alike but differ in meaning.
Regular verbs add -ed for the past; irregular verbs change.
Traditional games build strength and teamwork.
